title: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation:  Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
summary: Deep learning regression and classification tools typically do not capture model uncertainty, whereas Bayesian models do but at prohibitive computational cost. The paper casts dropout training in neural networks as approximate variational inference in deep Gaussian processes, yielding MC dropout: averaging T stochastic forward passes to estimate predictive mean and variance. On UCI regression benchmarks, notably Boston Housing, MC dropout improves test RMSE and predictive log-likelihood over VI and probabilistic back-propagation, achieving 2.97 ± 0.19 RMSE on Boston Housing in the 20-split setting.

why: The authors' repo is cloned and contains the entire experimental apparatus: experiment.py, net/net.py, and all UCI_Datasets directories with data.txt, the exact 20 train/test index splits, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs/n_hidden configs, plus the authors' published result files (test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt etc.) for direct comparison. Nothing data- or weight-wise is missing (models are trained from scratch). What is broken is the runtime: the code targets Keras 2.2.0 on Theano 0.8.2 (README), Theano is unmaintained and not installable on Python 3.12, TF1.x/Keras 2.2 wheels do not exist for Python 3.12, and 9 of 11 Python files are Python-2 style. So we keep the authors' logic (architecture, dropout rates, epochs, tau/grid-search protocol, per-split train/val selection) but port the training/evaluation core to a modern framework and run the same splits.
est_runtime: Port work: ~20-30 min (rewrite net/net.py + experiment.py training/MC-dropout loop in a modern framework, keep split loading and grid-search logic). Runs (Boston Housing, 1x50 net, 400 epochs, batch 32, per-split grid over the repo's dropout_rates/tau_values, T MC forward passes): ~10-15 s per model fit on 22 CPU cores, so ~2-4 min per split with grid search. Full 20-split C1 protocol is ~40-80 min of compute, i.e. borderline-to-over the ~60 min total budget once the port is included.
scale_down_plan: Keep the exact released protocol but shrink along the split axis, not the model axis: evaluate the first 5 of the 20 released Boston Housing splits (index_train_*/index_test_*), same 1-hidden-layer/50-unit net, same dropout rates, same l=1e-2, same per-split train/val grid over tau, same 10x epochs (400), batch 32, Adam, T MC forward passes. Report mean test RMSE with standard error over 5 splits and state the split count explicitly. Secondary cheap confirmation on Yacht Hydrodynamics (N=308, <1 min/split) if time permits. Expected effect on the number: the point estimate should land near the released 2.83-2.97 range within a much wider error bar (SE roughly sqrt(20/5)~2x larger, i.e. +/-0.3-0.4 instead of +/-0.19); the qualitative claim (MC dropout beats VI, comparable-to-better than PBP 3.01) remains testable, but the printed +/-0.19 cannot be matched with 5 splits. If the port finishes fast, extend toward 10-20 splits; do not cut epochs or MC samples first, since those change the estimator itself.
blockers: code targets Theano 0.8.2 + Keras 2.2.0; Theano is dead and cannot be installed on Python 3.12
Keras 2.2.0 / TensorFlow 1.x have no wheels for Python 3.12 (and Keras 3 API differs: layer-level train-time dropout loops, .compile/.fit behaviour, model saving)
9 of 11 python files are Python-2 style (print statements, old import style) and need 2to3-style edits even before framework porting
no GPU on this machine; README launch command assumes device=gpu + float32 (not fatal: the UCI nets are tiny and the paper reports CPU-class runtimes, e.g. naval 276 s/split incl. BO)
protocol requires a per-split train/val split + grid search over dropout rate and tau before the final train, so per-split cost is much larger than a single 400-epoch fit

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction: we keep the authors' released data and the exact 20 per-split train/test index files from https://github.com/yaringal/DropoutUncertaintyExps (bostonHousing/data/data.txt, index_train_i.txt, index_test_i.txt, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs.txt, n_hidden.txt) and their grid-search-over-dropout-rate-and-tau protocol, but re-implement the 1-hidden-layer/50-unit dropout network plus the MC-dropout training/evaluation loop in PyTorch (CPU) because the original Keras 2.2.0 + Theano 0.8.2 stack and its Python-2 source cannot run on Python 3.12 (this is the single documented deviation from R13). For each of the first 5 of the 20 released Boston Housing splits we carve an 80/20 train/validation split from the training indices, grid-search dropout rate and tau by validation log-likelihood, set the L2 weight decay from the searched tau and l=1e-2 via the eq.(7) relation exactly as coded in net/net.py, train the final model for the fixed epoch budget (10x the base schedule, ~400 epochs, no early stopping) with Adam/batch-32, and evaluate test RMSE (inverse-transformed to original target units) and predictive log-likelihood with T=1000 MC-dropout stochastic forward passes. reproduce.py aggregates mean±standard-error over the 5 splits, writes results/metrics.json, and prints the authors' released per-split result files for direct comparison. The expected point estimate is ~2.83-2.97 (inside the 0.19 tolerance around C1=2.97) but with a roughly 2x wider standard error (5 of 20 splits), so the honest verdict is partially_reproduced.
steps: 1. Environment: verify python>=3.12, numpy/scipy/pandas/scikit-learn present, then `pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu` (CPU wheel) and `python -c "import torch;print(torch.__version__)"`. Do NOT attempt to install Theano/Keras 2.2/TF1 - they are uninstallable on 3.12 (documented blocker; deviation from R13).

2. Repo check: confirm DropoutUncertaintyExps/ is present; assert existence of UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing/data/{data.txt, index_features.txt, index_target.txt, dropout_rates.txt, tau_values.txt, n_epochs.txt, n_hidden.txt, n_splits.txt} and index_train_0..19.txt / index_test_0..19.txt, plus results/ releasing test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt.

3. Read experiment.py and net/net.py end-to-end; write down (in a notes file or docstring) the exact protocol: how the 80/20 train-val split is formed, how (dropout_rate, tau) are grid-searched and scored, how weight decay lambda is derived from tau/l/N, the exact epoch count and multiplier, and how RMSE and eq.(8) log-likelihood are computed. This dictation of the authors' logic is what the PyTorch port must mirror.
4. Parse the bostonHousing data dir config files and print them (dropout rates, tau values, n_epochs, n_hidden, n_splits, index_features, index_target) so the counts drive the grid size.
5. Write config.py with the values above (paper/assumption tags inline).
6. Write data_utils.py: load_data(split) -> (X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val, X_test, y_test, scaler_y); standardize X and y on train statistics; verbose shapes. No torch import needed here.
7. Write model.py: DropoutRegressor(Q, hidden=50, p_in, p_out) with dropout before each weight layer; keep_dropout_at_eval flag.

8. Write mc_dropout.py: compute_lambda(tau,l,N) reading net/net.py's formula; train_model(...) (Adam lr=1e-3, batch 32, fixed epochs, shuffled); mc_predict(model, X, T=1000) -> mean, variance; rmse_inverse(y, yhat_mean, scaler_y); predictive_log_likelihood(...) per eq.(8)/net.py; grid_search(...) scoring by validation LL.

9. Write reproduce.py: iterate config.full_split_list, run grid search then final train then MC test eval, store per-split results, compute mean and SE = std/sqrt(n), set within_tolerance = |mean - 2.97| <= 0.19, dump results/metrics.json including split count, config snapshot, and the authors' released values.
10. Write compare_with_released.py to read the authors' results/*_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt files and print alongside ours.
11. Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) and fix any that fail before the full run.
12. Smoke test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` (split 0, 2 epochs, T=10, 1 grid point, 64 samples) - assert finite RMSE/LL, correct tensor shapes, <60 s.
13. Full run: `python reproduce.py --dataset bostonHousing --split-count 5` -> 5 splits x (grid search + 10x-epoch final train + T=1000 MC eval).
14. Inspect results/metrics.json: mean RMSE vs 2.97 with tolerance 0.19; compare to the authors' released 2.83/2.90; confirm the printed SE is ~2x the paper's because only 5 of 20 splits are used.
15. If budget remains after the 5-split Boston run, add a cheap secondary confirmation on Yacht Hydrodynamics (N=308), same protocol, and append it to metrics.json.

16. Write a short summary block into results/metrics.json stating the deviation (5/20 splits, grid-search instead of BO, PyTorch instead of Keras/Theano) and the resulting verdict (partially_reproduced).
smoke_test: `python reproduce.py --smoke` runs only split 0 on the first 64 training rows for 2 epochs with T=10 MC forward passes and a single (dropout,tau) grid point; it asserts the data loader returns correctly shaped train/val/test arrays, the net has 751 parameters, training losses are finite and decreasing, MC predictions have shape (n_test,) with non-negative variance, and RMSE/log-likelihood are finite scalars. It writes results/smoke_metrics.json and must finish in under ~60 s, proving the full data->train->MC-eval->JSON flow before the expensive run.
intermediate_checks: Data integrity: data.txt has 506 rows and Q columns equal to index_features.txt; index_train_i.txt and index_test_i.txt are disjoint and their union is all 506 indices; every index is in range.
Split hygiene: the 80/20 validation set is drawn only from training indices, disjoint from the test indices, and reproducible from the fixed seed (A3/A8).
Grid files parse: dropout_rates.txt and tau_values.txt yield the expected number of values (print them); grid size = len(rates)*len(taus).
Parameter count: 13*50+50 + 50*1+1 = 751 parameters; print and assert this matches the instantiated model.

Weight-decay sanity: print lambda for the searched tau values and N=train size; assert lambda > 0 and varies monotonically with tau as eq.(7)/net.py implies; verify lambda matches net/net.py's formula on a hand-computed example.
Target scaling: after standardization the train target has mean~0, std~1; inverse_transform(standardize(y))==y within 1e-8.

Sanity baseline: fit a plain (dropout-off at eval, or a least-squares linear) model on split 0 and confirm test RMSE is in a plausible Boston range (~3-6), i.e. the pipeline is not degenerate before the dropout run.

Authors' anchor: read UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing/results/test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt and record the released per-split RMSEs (expect point estimate ~2.83-2.97) so our numbers can be compared immediately after the full run.
budget_plan: Total ~60 min. Setup + reading experiment.py/net.py + writing the PyTorch port: ~15-20 min. Intermediate checks: ~5 min. Smoke test: ~1-2 min. Full 5-split Boston Housing run (grid search + 400-epoch final train + T=1000 MC eval, ~2-4 min/split on the CPU cores): ~10-20 min. Aggregation, comparison to released files, and writing results/metrics.json: ~5 min. Remaining ~5-10 min reserved as buffer; if the port finished fast and the buffer is intact, extend the split list toward 10 before considering any reduction of epochs or T (the route forbids shrinking the estimator).

"""Quick timing benchmark: one 400-epoch fit of the 1x50 dropout net on Boston Housing."""
import time
import numpy as np
import torch

torch.set_num_threads(1)

d = 'repo/UCI_Datasets/bostonHousing/data/'
data = np.loadtxt(d + 'data.txt')
print('data shape', data.shape)
X = data[:, :13]
y = data[:, 13]
idx_tr = np.loadtxt(d + 'index_train_0.txt').astype(int)
idx_te = np.loadtxt(d + 'index_test_0.txt').astype(int)
print('train', len(idx_tr), 'test', len(idx_te), 'union', len(set(idx_tr) | set(idx_te)))

Xtr, ytr = X[idx_tr], y[idx_tr]
n_tr = int(0.8 * Xtr.shape[0])
Xfit, yfit = Xtr[:n_tr], ytr[:n_tr]

mu, sd = Xfit.mean(0), Xfit.std(0)
sd[sd == 0] = 1
Xf = (Xfit - mu) / sd
ymu, ysd = yfit.mean(), yfit.std()
yf = (yfit - ymu) / ysd

dev = 'cpu'
Xt = torch.tensor(Xf, dtype=torch.float32)
Yt = torch.tensor(yf[:, None], dtype=torch.float32)

model = torch.nn.Sequential(torch.nn.Dropout(0.05), torch.nn.Linear(13, 50),
                            torch.nn.ReLU(), torch.nn.Dropout(0.05), torch.nn.Linear(50, 1))
torch.nn.init.xavier_uniform_(model[1].weight); torch.nn.init.zeros_(model[1].bias)
torch.nn.init.xavier_uniform_(model[4].weight); torch.nn.init.zeros_(model[4].bias)
opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
reg = 1e-2 ** 2 * (1 - 0.05) / (2. * n_tr * 0.1)
lossf = torch.nn.MSELoss()


def fit(epochs, batch):
    n = Xt.shape[0]
    t0 = time.time()
    model.train()
    for ep in range(epochs):
        perm = torch.randperm(n)
        for i in range(0, n, batch):
            sl = perm[i:i + batch]
            opt.zero_grad()
            pred = model(Xt[sl])
            loss = lossf(pred, Yt[sl])
            pen = sum(reg * (p ** 2).sum() for p in model.parameters() if p.dim() == 2)
            (loss + pen).backward()
            opt.step()
    return time.time() - t0


print('reg', reg)
t = fit(50, 32)
print('50 epochs bs32: %.2fs -> 400 epochs est %.1fs' % (t, t * 8))
t = fit(400, 32)
print('400 epochs bs32: %.2fs' % t)

# MC prediction timing
Xte = torch.tensor((X[idx_te] - mu) / sd, dtype=torch.float32)
T = 1000
model.train()
t0 = time.time()
with torch.no_grad():
    outs = []
    for t in range(T):
        outs.append(model(Xte))
    outs = torch.stack(outs)
print('T=1000 loop MC: %.2fs' % (time.time() - t0))

# vectorised MC: (T, n, 13)
t0 = time.time()
with torch.no_grad():
    W1, b1 = model[1].weight, model[1].bias
    W2, b2 = model[4].weight, model[4].bias
    n = Xte.shape[0]
    Xb = Xte.expand(T, n, 13)
    Xb = torch.nn.functional.dropout(Xb, 0.05, True)
    H = torch.nn.functional.relu(Xb @ W1.T + b1)
    H = torch.nn.functional.dropout(H, 0.05, True)
    P = H @ W2.T + b2
print('T=1000 vectorised MC: %.3fs shape %s' % (time.time() - t0, tuple(P.shape)))

"""Data loading for the UCI regression benchmarks, mirroring repo/experiment.py.

Everything here is numpy-only (no torch) so it can be unit-tested independently.
"""
import os

import numpy as np

import config

DATA_DIR = lambda ds: os.path.join(config.UCI_ROOT, ds, "data")  # noqa: E731


def _load_vector(path):
    """np.loadtxt of a one-column-per-line file -> python list (as in experiment.py)."""
    return np.loadtxt(path).tolist()


def load_grid(dataset):
    """Return (dropout_rates, tau_values) exactly as read from the repo's data dir."""
    d = DATA_DIR(dataset)
    rates = _load_vector(os.path.join(d, "dropout_rates.txt"))
    taus = _load_vector(os.path.join(d, "tau_values.txt"))
    if np.ndim(rates) == 0:
        rates = [float(rates)]
    if np.ndim(taus) == 0:
        taus = [float(taus)]
    return [float(r) for r in rates], [float(t) for t in taus]


def load_meta(dataset):
    d = DATA_DIR(dataset)
    return dict(
        n_hidden=int(_load_vector(os.path.join(d, "n_hidden.txt"))),
        n_epochs=int(_load_vector(os.path.join(d, "n_epochs.txt"))),
        n_splits=int(_load_vector(os.path.join(d, "n_splits.txt"))),
    )


def load_xy(dataset):
    """Full (X, y) matrix from data.txt using index_features.txt / index_target.txt."""
    d = DATA_DIR(dataset)
    data = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "data.txt"))
    index_features = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "index_features.txt"))
    index_target = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "index_target.txt"))
    X = data[:, [int(i) for i in np.atleast_1d(index_features).tolist()]]
    y = data[:, int(float(index_target))]
    return X, y


def split_indices(dataset, split):
    d = DATA_DIR(dataset)
    tr = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "index_train_%d.txt" % split)).astype(int)
    te = np.loadtxt(os.path.join(d, "index_test_%d.txt" % split)).astype(int)
    return tr, te


def check_split(dataset, split, n_rows):
    """Data-integrity check: disjoint train/test, union == whole data set, in range."""
    tr, te = split_indices(dataset, split)
    assert tr.min() >= 0 and te.min() >= 0, "negative index"
    assert tr.max() < n_rows and te.max() < n_rows, "index out of range"
    assert len(set(tr.tolist()) & set(te.tolist())) == 0, "train/test overlap"
    assert len(set(tr.tolist()) | set(te.tolist())) == n_rows, "train+test != all rows"
    return tr, te


def train_val_slice(X_tr, y_tr, val_fraction=config.VAL_FRACTION):
    """repo/experiment.py lines 132-136: deterministic 80/20 slice of the index order."""
    n = int(val_fraction * X_tr.shape[0])          # int() truncates, as in the repo
    return X_tr[:n], y_tr[:n], X_tr[n:], y_tr[n:]


class Scaler:
    """The normalization performed inside repo/net/net.py (population std, ddof=0)."""

    def __init__(self, X, y):
        self.mean_X = np.mean(X, 0)
        self.std_X = np.std(X, 0)
        self.std_X[self.std_X == 0] = 1
        self.mean_y = np.mean(y)
        self.std_y = np.std(y)

    def transform(self, X, y=None):
        Xn = (X - self.mean_X) / self.std_X
        if y is None:
            return Xn
        return Xn, (np.asarray(y) - self.mean_y) / self.std_y

    def inverse_y(self, y_norm):
        return np.asarray(y_norm) * self.std_y + self.mean_y


def get_split_data(dataset, split, smoke_n=None, seed=0):
    """Return dict with train/val/test arrays (raw, un-normalised) for one split."""
    X, y = load_xy(dataset)
    tr, te = check_split(dataset, split, X.shape[0])
    X_tr_all, y_tr_all = X[tr], y[tr]
    X_te, y_te = X[te], y[te]
    X_fit, y_fit, X_val, y_val = train_val_slice(X_tr_all, y_tr_all)
    if smoke_n:
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        sel = rng.choice(X_fit.shape[0], size=min(smoke_n, X_fit.shape[0]), replace=False)
        X_fit, y_fit = X_fit[sel], y_fit[sel]
    return dict(X_fit=X_fit, y_fit=y_fit, X_val=X_val, y_val=y_val,
                X_train_all=X_tr_all, y_train_all=y_tr_all, X_test=X_te, y_test=y_te,
                n_features=X.shape[1], n_rows=X.shape[0])

"""The Table-1 dropout regression network, in pure NumPy.

Architecture (repo/net/net.py, num_hidden_layers=1):

    x -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(50, relu, l2(reg)) -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(1, l2(reg))

i.e. dropout is applied *before every weight layer* [PAPER R2] with a single rate p
that is grid-searched (the repo uses one rate for all layers; the paper text quotes
0.05 and 0.005, both of which are inside the released dropout_rates.txt grid).

Two deliberate implementation choices:

* Dropout is kept ON for prediction as well.  The released code builds the Keras
  graph with `Dropout(p)(inputs, training=True)`, which forces the learning phase to
  train, so `model.predict` is itself a stochastic forward pass.  That is exactly the
  MC-dropout sampler of eq. (6) [PAPER R8].
* NumPy instead of Keras/Theano: the released stack (Theano 0.8.2 + Keras 2.2.0) is
  not installable on Python 3.12.  The tiny 13-50-1 net is ~30x faster in NumPy than
  in per-op PyTorch, which is what lets the full 20-split grid search fit the budget.
  The math (forward/backward/Adam) is validated against torch in tests_check.py.
"""
import numpy as np


def glorot_uniform(shape, rng):
    """Keras `glorot_uniform` kernel initializer: U(-a, a), a = sqrt(6/(fan_in+fan_out))."""
    fan_in, fan_out = shape[0], shape[1]
    limit = np.sqrt(6.0 / (fan_in + fan_out))
    return rng.uniform(-limit, limit, size=shape)


class DropoutNet:
    """1 hidden layer of `n_hidden` relu units, dropout before every weight layer."""

    def __init__(self, n_in, n_hidden, dropout, reg, seed=0, n_layers=1):
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        self.dropout = float(dropout)
        self.reg = float(reg)          # Keras l2(reg): penalty = reg * sum(w^2)
        self.n_layers = int(n_layers)
        self.n_hidden = int(n_hidden)
        sizes = [n_in] + [self.n_hidden] * self.n_layers + [1]
        self.W, self.b = [], []
        for i in range(len(sizes) - 1):
            self.W.append(glorot_uniform((sizes[i], sizes[i + 1]), rng))
            self.b.append(np.zeros(sizes[i + 1]))
        self.params = list(zip(self.W, self.b))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- forward
    def _forward(self, X, rng, train=True):
        """Returns (output, cache) with dropout applied before every weight layer."""
        a, masks = X, []
        for i, (W, b) in enumerate(self.params):
            if self.dropout > 0:
                m = (rng.rand(*a.shape) >= self.dropout) / (1.0 - self.dropout)
            else:
                m = 1.0
            masks.append(m)
            z = (a * m) @ W + b
            if i < len(self.params) - 1:
                a = np.maximum(z, 0.0)          # relu on hidden layers
            else:
                a = z                            # linear output
        return a, masks

    def predict_pass(self, X, rng):
        """One stochastic (MC-dropout) forward pass, dropout ON [PAPER R8]."""
        return self._forward(X, rng)[0]

    def loss_and_grads(self, X, y, rng):
        """Mean squared error over the batch + reg*sum(w^2) on every kernel.

        Mirrors Keras: loss = mean((f(x)-y)^2) + sum_l l2_l2_reg_l * ||W_l||^2 .
        """
        n = X.shape[0]
        out, masks = self._forward(X, rng)
        resid = out - y
        mse = float(np.mean(resid ** 2))
        loss = mse + self.reg * sum(float(np.sum(W ** 2)) for W in self.W)

        gW = [np.zeros_like(W) for W in self.W]
        gb = [np.zeros_like(b) for b in self.b]
        d = 2.0 * resid / n                       # d(mean sq err)/d(out)
        for i in range(len(self.params) - 1, -1, -1):
            a_prev = X if i == 0 else self._act_cache[i - 1]
            d = d * masks[i]                      # backward through the dropout mask
            gW[i] = a_prev.T @ d + 2.0 * self.reg * self.W[i]
            gb[i] = d.sum(0)
            if i > 0:
                d = (d @ self.W[i].T > 0) * d     # relu backward
        self._act_cache = None
        return loss, gW, gb

    def fit(self, X, y, n_epochs, batch_size, rng, shuffle=True):
        """Adam(1e-3) training loop, fixed epoch budget, no early stopping [R5,R6,R12]."""
        lr, b1, b2, eps = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
        mW = [np.zeros_like(W) for W in self.W]
        vW = [np.zeros_like(W) for W in self.W]
        mb = [np.zeros_like(b) for b in self.b]
        vb = [np.zeros_like(b) for b in self.b]
        t = 0
        n = X.shape[0]
        for epoch in range(n_epochs):
            if shuffle:
                order = rng.permutation(n)
                Xs, ys = X[order], y[order]
            else:
                Xs, ys = X, y
            for start in range(0, n, batch_size):
                Xb, yb = Xs[start:start + batch_size], ys[start:start + batch_size]
                self._act_cache = self._acts(Xb, rng)
                _, gW, gb = self.loss_and_grads(Xb, yb, rng)
                t += 1
                for k in range(len(self.params)):
                    for store, grad, p in ((mW, gW, self.W), (mb, gb, self.b)):
                        s = store[k]
                        s *= b1
                        s += (1 - b1) * grad[k]
                        v = vW[k] if store is mW else vb[k]
                        v *= b2
                        v += (1 - b2) * grad[k] ** 2
                        mh = s / (1 - b1 ** t)
                        vh = v / (1 - b2 ** t)
                        p -= lr * mh / (np.sqrt(vh) + eps)
        return self

    def _acts(self, X, rng):
        """Activations entering each weight layer (needed for the weight gradients)."""
        cache, a = [], X
        for i, (W, b) in enumerate(self.params):
            cache.append(a)
            if i < len(self.params) - 1:
                a = np.maximum((a * (rng.rand(*a.shape) >= self.dropout) /
                               (1.0 - self.dropout)) @ W + b, 0.0)
        return cache

"""The Table-1 dropout regression network, in pure NumPy.

Architecture (repo/net/net.py with num_hidden_layers=1):

    x -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(50, relu, l2(reg)) -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(1, l2(reg))

so dropout is applied *before every weight layer* [PAPER R2] with one rate p that is
grid-searched.  The released code uses a single rate for all layers; the paper text
quotes "probabilities 0.05 and 0.005", and both values are entries of the released
data/dropout_rates.txt grid {0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1}.

Two deliberate implementation choices:

* Dropout stays ON for prediction.  The released code builds the Keras graph with
  `Dropout(p)(inputs, training=True)`, which forces the learning phase to train, so
  even `model.predict` is a stochastic forward pass -- exactly the MC-dropout sampler
  of eq. (6) [PAPER R8].
* NumPy instead of Keras/Theano: the released stack (Theano 0.8.2 + Keras 2.2.0) is
  not installable on Python 3.12.  For this tiny 13-50-1 net NumPy is far cheaper per
  step than framework overhead, which is what lets the full 20-split grid search fit
  the time budget.  The forward/backward/Adam math is checked against torch.nn in
  tests_check.py.
"""
import numpy as np

ADAM_LR, ADAM_B1, ADAM_B2, ADAM_EPS = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8   # Keras Adam defaults [R6/A6]


def glorot_uniform(shape, rng):
    """Keras `glorot_uniform` kernel init: U(-a, a), a = sqrt(6/(fan_in+fan_out)) [A9]."""
    limit = np.sqrt(6.0 / (shape[0] + shape[1]))
    return rng.uniform(-limit, limit, size=shape)


class DropoutNet:
    def __init__(self, n_in, n_hidden, dropout, reg, seed=0, n_layers=1):
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        self.dropout = float(dropout)
        self.reg = float(reg)          # Keras l2(reg): penalty = reg * sum(W^2) [R3/eq.7]
        sizes = [int(n_in)] + [int(n_hidden)] * int(n_layers) + [1]
        self.W = [glorot_uniform((sizes[i], sizes[i + 1]), rng) for i in range(len(sizes) - 1)]
        self.b = [np.zeros(s) for s in sizes[1:]]
        self.n_params = sum(w.size for w in self.W) + sum(b.size for b in self.b)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ forward
    def _forward(self, X, rng, with_masks=True):
        """Returns (out, act_in, masks). act_in[i] is the input of weight layer i."""
        act_in, masks = [], []
        a = X
        for i, (W, b) in enumerate(zip(self.W, self.b)):
            act_in.append(a)
            if self.dropout > 0 and with_masks:
                m = (rng.rand(*a.shape) >= self.dropout) / (1.0 - self.dropout)
            else:
                m = 1.0
            masks.append(m)
            z = (a * m) @ W + b
            a = np.maximum(z, 0.0) if i < len(self.W) - 1 else z
        return a, act_in, masks

    def step(self, X, y, rng):
        """Loss and gradients for one mini-batch (same forward pass as the loss).

        Keras objective reproduced: mean((f(x)-y)^2) + reg * sum_l ||W_l||^2,
        with the regularizer added to the *mean* batch loss.
        """
        n = X.shape[0]
        out, act_in, masks = self._forward(X, rng)
        resid = out - y
        mse = float(np.mean(resid ** 2))
        pen = self.reg * sum(float(np.sum(W ** 2)) for W in self.W)
        grads = []
        d = 2.0 * resid / n
        for i in range(len(self.W) - 1, -1, -1):
            d = d * masks[i]                       # backward through this layer's mask
            gW = act_in[i].T @ d + 2.0 * self.reg * self.W[i]
            gb = d.sum(0)
            grads.append((gW, gb))
            if i > 0:
                d = (d @ self.W[i].T) * (d @ self.W[i].T > 0)   # relu backward
        grads.reverse()
        return mse + pen, mse, grads

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- train
    def fit(self, X, y, n_epochs, batch_size, rng, shuffle=True):
        """Fixed epoch budget, no early stopping [R5, R12]; Adam + shuffled mini-batches [R6]."""
        mW = [np.zeros_like(w) for w in self.W]
        vW = [np.zeros_like(w) for w in self.W]
        mb = [np.zeros_like(x) for x in self.b]
        vb = [np.zeros_like(x) for x in self.b]
        t = 0
        n = X.shape[0]
        losses = []
        for epoch in range(int(n_epochs)):
            if shuffle:
                order = rng.permutation(n)
                Xs, ys = X[order], y[order]
            else:
                Xs, ys = X, y
            for start in range(0, n, batch_size):
                Xb, yb = Xs[start:start + batch_size], ys[start:start + batch_size]
                _, mse, grads = self.step(Xb, yb, rng)
                t += 1
                for k in range(len(self.W)):
                    for P, G, M, V in ((self.W, grads[k][0], mW, vW),
                                       (self.b, grads[k][1], mb, vb)):
                        M[k] = ADAM_B1 * M[k] + (1 - ADAM_B1) * G
                        V[k] = ADAM_B2 * V[k] + (1 - ADAM_B2) * G ** 2
                        mh = M[k] / (1 - ADAM_B1 ** t)
                        vh = V[k] / (1 - ADAM_B2 ** t)
                        P[k] -= ADAM_LR * mh / (np.sqrt(vh) + ADAM_EPS)
            if n_epochs <= 10 or (epoch + 1) % max(1, n_epochs // 10) == 0:
                losses.append((epoch + 1, mse))
        self.loss_curve = losses
        return self

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- MC dropout
    def mc_predict(self, X, T, rng, chunk=1000):
        """T stochastic forward passes [R8].  Returns (T, n, 1) predictions."""
        outs = []
        for start in range(0, T, chunk):
            c = min(chunk, T - start)
            Xb = np.repeat(X[None, :, :], c, axis=0)          # (c, n, d)
            a = Xb
            for i, (W, b) in enumerate(zip(self.W, self.b)):
                if self.dropout > 0:
                    m = (rng.rand(*a.shape) >= self.dropout) / (1.0 - self.dropout)
                    a = a * m
                z = a @ W + b
                a = np.maximum(z, 0.0) if i < len(self.W) - 1 else z

"""Ported core of repo/net/net.py + repo/experiment.py (see notes in each function).

Everything here mirrors the authors' released logic; only the framework is NumPy.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.special import logsumexp

import config
import data_utils
from model import DropoutNet


def weight_decay(lengthscale, dropout, N, tau):
    """repo/net/net.py line 72:  reg = lengthscale**2 * (1 - dropout) / (2. * N * tau).

    This is the paper's eq. (7) relation between prior length-scale l, model precision
    tau, data size N and the L2 weight decay [R3].
    """
    return lengthscale ** 2 * (1.0 - dropout) / (2.0 * N * tau)


def mc_log_likelihood(y, Y_hat, tau):
    """eq. (8) / repo/net/net.py lines 134-136, computed in ORIGINAL target units.

    log p(y*|x*) ~= logsumexp_t( -0.5*tau*(y - f_t(x))^2 ) - log T - 0.5*log(2 pi) + 0.5*log tau
    """
    y = np.asarray(y).reshape(1, -1, 1)
    diff = y - Y_hat
    T = Y_hat.shape[0]
    ll = (logsumexp(-0.5 * tau * diff.astype(np.float64) ** 2, axis=0).ravel()
          - np.log(T) - 0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) + 0.5 * np.log(tau))
    return ll


def evaluate(model, scaler, X, y, T, rng_seed):
    """repo/net/net.py `predict`: one plain pass + T MC passes, RMSE and eq.(8) LL."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(rng_seed)
    Xn, yn = scaler.transform(X, y)
    Yt = model.mc_predict(Xn, T, rng, chunk=config.T_MC_CHUNK)      # (T, n, 1)
    Yt = scaler.inverse_y(Yt)                                        # back to original units
    mc_mean = Yt.mean(axis=0).ravel()
    rmse_mc = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((y - mc_mean) ** 2)))            # eq. (6) [R8]
    single = Yt[0].ravel()
    rmse_single = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((y - single) ** 2)))         # repo's "standard_pred"
    ll = float(np.mean(mc_log_likelihood(y, Yt, model.tau)))         # [R9]
    return dict(rmse=rmse_mc, rmse_single=rmse_single, ll=ll,
                pred_mean=mc_mean, pred_var=Yt.var(axis=0).ravel())


def train_net(X_fit, y_fit, dropout, tau, n_epochs, seed, n_hidden=None, dataset=None):
    """The released `net` constructor: normalize, build, fit, done (no early stopping)."""
    scaler = data_utils.Scaler(X_fit, y_fit)
    Xn, yn = scaler.transform(X_fit, y_fit)
    yn = yn.reshape(-1, 1)
    N = X_fit.shape[0]
    reg = weight_decay(config.LENGTHSCALE, dropout, N, tau)
    model = DropoutNet(X_fit.shape[1], n_hidden or config.N_HIDDEN_UNITS, dropout, reg,
                       seed=seed, n_layers=config.N_HIDDEN_LAYERS)
    model.tau = tau
    model.reg = reg
    model.N = N
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    model.fit(Xn, yn, n_epochs, config.BATCH_SIZE, rng, shuffle=config.SHUFFLE)
    return model, scaler


def grid_search(dataset, split, rates, taus, n_epochs, T, seed_base=0, log=None,
                subset_n=None):
    """repo/experiment.py lines 153-183: pick (dropout, tau) with the best *validation* LL.

    The winner's network is the one trained on the 80% train subset, exactly as in the
    released code (it is then re-trained from scratch on the full training set).
    """
    d = data_utils.get_split_data(dataset, split, smoke_n=subset_n)
    best = dict(ll=-float("inf"))
    for gi, p in enumerate(rates):
        for tau in taus:
            model, scaler = train_net(d["X_fit"], d["y_fit"], p, tau, n_epochs,
                                      seed=seed_base + 1000 * split + 17 * gi + int(tau * 100))
            res = evaluate(model, scaler, d["X_val"], d["y_val"], T,
                           rng_seed=seed_base + 7 + split)
            if log is not None:
                log.append(dict(split=split, dropout=p, tau=tau, val_rmse=res["rmse"],
                                val_ll=res["ll"]))
            if res["ll"] > best["ll"]:
                best = dict(ll=res["ll"], rmse=res["rmse"], dropout=p, tau=tau,
                            reg=model.reg, N=model.N)
    return best, d


def final_run(dataset, split, dropout, tau, n_epochs, T, seed_base=0):
    """repo/experiment.py lines 186-189: retrain on the WHOLE training set, test on test."""
    d = data_utils.get_split_data(dataset, split)
    model, scaler = train_net(d["X_train_all"], d["y_train_all"], dropout, tau, n_epochs,
                              seed=seed_base + 500 + split)
    res = evaluate(model, scaler, d["X_test"], d["y_test"], T, rng_seed=seed_base + 11 + split)
    res.update(dropout=dropout, tau=tau, reg=model.reg, N=model.N, split=split,
               n_train=d["X_train_all"].shape[0], n_val=d["X_val"].shape[0],
               n_test=d["X_test"].shape[0])
    return res

"""The Table-1 dropout regression network, in pure NumPy.

Architecture (repo/net/net.py with num_hidden_layers=1):

    x -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(50, relu, l2(reg)) -> Dropout(p) -> Dense(1, l2(reg))

so dropout is applied *before every weight layer* [PAPER R2] with one rate p that is
grid-searched over the released data/dropout_rates.txt grid {0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1}
(the paper text quotes "probabilities 0.05 and 0.005"; both are grid points, and the
released code ties the rate of every layer to one searched value).

Two deliberate implementation choices:

* Dropout stays ON for prediction.  The released code builds the Keras graph with
  `Dropout(p)(inputs, training=True)`, which forces the learning phase to train, so
  even `model.predict` is a stochastic forward pass -- exactly the MC-dropout sampler
  of eq. (6) [R8].
* NumPy instead of Keras/Theano: the released stack (Theano 0.8.2 + Keras 2.2.0) is
  not installable on Python 3.12.  For this tiny 13-50-1 net NumPy has far less
  per-step overhead than a framework, which is what lets the full 20-split grid
  search fit the time budget.  The forward/backward/Adam math is checked against
  torch.nn in tests_check.py.
"""
import numpy as np

from model_constants import ADAM_LR, ADAM_B1, ADAM_B2, ADAM_EPS


def glorot_uniform(shape, rng):
    """Keras default kernel_initializer='glorot_uniform'."""
    fan_in, fan_out = shape[0], shape[1]
    limit = np.sqrt(6.0 / (fan_in + fan_out))
    return rng.uniform(-limit, limit, size=shape).astype(np.float64)


class DropoutNet:
    """input -> Dropout -> Dense(hidden, relu) -> Dropout -> Dense(1)."""

    def __init__(self, n_in, n_hidden=50, dropout=0.05, reg=0.0, seed=0, n_layers=1):
        rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        self.dropout = float(dropout)
        self.reg = float(reg)
        sizes = [n_in] + [n_hidden] * int(n_layers) + [1]
        self.W, self.b = [], []
        for i in range(len(sizes) - 1):
            self.W.append(glorot_uniform((sizes[i], sizes[i + 1]), rng))
            self.b.append(np.zeros(sizes[i + 1]))
        self.mW = [np.zeros_like(w) for w in self.W]
        self.vW = [np.zeros_like(w) for w in self.W]
        self.mb = [np.zeros_like(v) for v in self.b]
        self.vb = [np.zeros_like(v) for v in self.b]
        self.t = 0
        self.keep = [1.0 - self.dropout] * len(self.W)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ forward
    def _forward(self, X, rng):
        """Return (out, act_in, masks); act_in[i] is the pre-dropout input of layer i."""
        a = X
        act_in = []
        masks = []
        d = self.dropout
        for i, W in enumerate(self.W):
            act_in.append(a)
            if d > 0.0:
                m = (rng.random_sample(a.shape) >= d) * self.keep[i]
            else:
                m = None
            masks.append(m)
            z = (a * m if m is not None else a) @ W + self.b[i]
            a = np.maximum(z, 0.0) if i < len(self.W) - 1 else z
        return a, act_in, masks

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ training
    def step(self, X, y, rng):
        """One mini-batch: MC-dropout forward, analytic backward, Adam update."""
        n = X.shape[0]
        out, act_in, masks = self._forward(X, rng)
        resid = out - y
        mse = float(resid.T @ resid)[0] / n
        pen = 0.0
        for W in self.W:
            pen += float(np.sum(W * W))
        pen *= self.reg
        grads = [None] * len(self.W)
        d = (2.0 / n) * resid                    # dL/dz of the (linear) output layer
        for i in range(len(self.W) - 1, -1, -1):
            h = act_in[i] if masks[i] is None else act_in[i] * masks[i]
            grads[i] = (h.T @ d + 2.0 * self.reg * self.W[i], d.sum(0))
            if i > 0:                            # back-prop through relu and this mask
                d = (d @ self.W[i].T) * masks[i] * (act_in[i] > 0)
        self._adam(grads)
        return mse + pen, mse

    def _adam(self, grads):
        self.t += 1
        t = self.t
        c1 = 1.0 - ADAM_B1 ** t
        c2 = 1.0 - ADAM_B2 ** t
        step_size = ADAM_LR / c1
        for i in range(len(self.W)):
            for P, G, M, V in ((self.W, grads[i][0], self.mW[i], self.vW[i]),
                               (self.b, grads[i][1], self.mb[i], self.vb[i])):
                M *= ADAM_B1
                M += (1.0 - ADAM_B1) * G
                V *= ADAM_B2
                V += (1.0 - ADAM_B2) * (G * G)
                P -= step_size * (M / (np.sqrt(V / c2) + ADAM_EPS))

    def fit(self, X, y, n_epochs, batch_size, rng, shuffle=True):
        n = X.shape[0]
        losses = []
        report = max(1, n_epochs // 10)
        for epoch in range(n_epochs):
            if shuffle:
                order = rng.permutation(n)
                Xs, ys = X[order], y[order]
            else:
                Xs, ys = X, y
            for s in range(0, n, batch_size):
                _, mse = self.step(Xs[s:s + batch_size], ys[s:s + batch_size], rng)
            if (epoch + 1) % report == 0 or epoch + 1 == n_epochs:
                losses.append((epoch + 1, mse))
        return losses

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- evaluation
    def mc_predict(self, X, T, rng, chunk=1000):
        """T independent stochastic forward passes [R8]; returns (T, n, 1) float64."""
        outs = []
        for start in range(0, T, chunk):
            c = min(chunk, T - start)
            a = np.repeat(X[None, :, :], c, axis=0)
            for i, W in enumerate(self.W):
                if self.dropout > 0.0:
                    a = a * ((rng.random_sample(a.shape) >= self.dropout) * self.keep[i])
                z = a @ W + self.b[i]
                a = np.maximum(z, 0.0) if i < len(self.W) - 1 else z
            outs.append(a)
        return np.concatenate(outs, axis=0)

"""Ported core of repo/net/net.py + repo/experiment.py (see notes in each function).

Everything here mirrors the authors' released logic; only the framework is NumPy.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.special import logsumexp

import config
import data_utils
from model import DropoutNet


def weight_decay(lengthscale, dropout, N, tau):
    """repo/net/net.py:  reg = lengthscale**2 * (1 - dropout) / (2. * N * tau).

    This is the paper's eq. (7) relation between prior length-scale l, model precision
    tau, data size N and the L2 weight decay [R3].
    """
    return lengthscale ** 2 * (1.0 - dropout) / (2.0 * N * tau)


def mc_log_likelihood(y, Y_hat, tau):
    """eq. (8) / repo/net/net.py, computed in ORIGINAL target units.

    log p(y*|x*) ~= logsumexp_t( -0.5*tau*(y - f_t(x))^2 ) - log T - 0.5*log(2 pi) + 0.5*log tau
    """
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64).reshape(1, -1, 1)
    diff = y - Y_hat
    T = Y_hat.shape[0]
    return (logsumexp(-0.5 * tau * diff ** 2, axis=0).ravel()
            - np.log(T) - 0.5 * np.log(2 * np.pi) + 0.5 * np.log(tau))


def evaluate(model, scaler, X, y, T, rng_seed):
    """MC dropout [R8/R9]: T stochastic passes -> mean, RMSE (original units), eq.(8) LL."""
    Xn, yn = scaler.transform(X, y)
    rng = np.random.RandomState(rng_seed)
    P = model.mc_predict(Xn, T, rng, chunk=config.MC_CHUNK)
    Y_hat = scaler.inverse_y(P)
    y_mean = Y_hat.mean(0)
    rmse = float(np.sqrt(np.mean((y_mean - np.asarray(y)) ** 2)))
    ll = float(np.mean(mc_log_likelihood(y, Y_hat, model.tau)))
    return dict(rmse=rmse, ll=ll, std=float(Y_hat.std(0).mean()))


def train_net(X_fit, y_fit, dropout, tau, n_epochs, seed, n_hidden=None, n_layers=None):
    """Mirror of net.py's constructor + fit(): normalise, set reg from (tau,l,N), train."""
    scaler = data_utils.Scaler(X_fit, y_fit)
    Xn, yn = scaler.transform(X_fit, y_fit)
    yn = yn.reshape(-1, 1)
    reg = weight_decay(config.LENGTHSCALE, dropout, X_fit.shape[0], tau)
    model = DropoutNet(X_fit.shape[1], n_hidden or config.N_HIDDEN_UNITS, dropout, reg,
                       seed=seed, n_layers=(n_layers or config.N_HIDDEN_LAYERS))
    model.tau = tau
    model.reg_value = reg
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed + 1)
    losses = model.fit(Xn, yn, n_epochs, config.BATCH_SIZE, rng, shuffle=config.SHUFFLE)
    return model, scaler, losses


def grid_search(data, rates, taus, n_epochs, seed_base, T=None):
    """experiment.py's search_for_parameters(): grid over (dropout, tau) by validation LL.

    The train/validation split is the released deterministic 80/20 slice of the training
    indices (experiment.py lines 86-91), and the score is mean eq.(8) log-likelihood on
    the validation set (experiment.py lines 164-172).
    """
    T = T or config.T_GRID
    rows = []
    for i, p in enumerate(rates):
        for j, tau in enumerate(taus):
            model, scaler, losses = train_net(
                data["X_fit"], data["y_fit"], p, tau, n_epochs, seed_base + 100 * i + j)
            r = evaluate(model, scaler, data["X_val"], data["y_val"], T, seed_base + 7000)
            rows.append(dict(dropout=p, tau=tau, val_ll=r["ll"], val_rmse=r["rmse"],
                             final_train_loss=losses[-1][1] if losses else None))
    best = max(rows, key=lambda r: r["val_ll"])
    return best, rows


def run_split(dataset, split, rates, taus, n_epochs, epochs_multiplier,
              T_test=None, skip_grid=False, selected=None, seed_base=None):
    """Full per-split protocol: grid search -> retrain on all training data -> MC test eval."""
    seed_base = seed_base if seed_base is not None else config.SEED_BASE + 1000 * split
    data = data_utils.get_split_data(dataset, split, config.VAL_FRACTION)
    T_test = T_test or config.T_TEST
    out = dict(split=split, dataset=dataset)
    if skip_grid:
        best = dict(dropout=selected["dropout"], tau=selected["tau"],
                    val_ll=selected.get("val_ll"), val_rmse=selected.get("val_rmse"))
        rows = None
    else:
        best, rows = grid_search(data, rates, taus, int(n_epochs * epochs_multiplier),
                                 seed_base, T=T_test if config.GRID_SAME_T_AS_TEST else None)
    # final model: trained on the WHOLE training set (train indices), same settings
    fm, fsc, flosses = train_net(data["X_train_all"], data["y_train_all"], best["dropout"],
                                 best["tau"], int(n_epochs * epochs_multiplier), seed_base)
    tr = evaluate(fm, fsc, data["X_train_all"], data["y_train_all"], T_test, seed_base + 3)
    te = evaluate(fm, fsc, data["X_test"], data["y_test"], T_test, seed_base + 4)
    out.update(best=best, grid=rows, test_rmse=te["rmse"], test_ll=te["ll"],
               train_rmse=tr["rmse"], mc_std=te["std"],
               final_train_loss=flosses[-1][1] if flosses else None)
    return out

"""Reproduce C1: MC-dropout test RMSE on Boston Housing (Table 1 of Gal 2015).

Usage
    python reproduce.py                       # full run (default: 20 released splits)
    python reproduce.py --split-count 5       # subset of the released splits
    python reproduce.py --search              # grid search only -> selected_config.json
    python reproduce.py --smoke               # tiny data-flow test, writes results/smoke_metrics.json

Protocol (ported from the authors' released code, repo/experiment.py + repo/net/net.py):
  per split: deterministic 80/20 train/val slice of the training indices
             -> grid search over dropout_rates.txt x tau_values.txt scored by the
                eq.(8) validation log-likelihood
             -> retrain on all training indices for EPOCH_MULTIPLIER x n_epochs.txt
                epochs (no early stopping) with Adam / batch 32
             -> T stochastic forward passes for test RMSE (eq. 6) and predictive LL (eq. 8).
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import time

import numpy as np

import config
import data_utils
import mc_dropout


def _workers(n_tasks):
    if config.N_WORKERS:
        return min(config.N_WORKERS, n_tasks)
    return max(1, min(6, (os.cpu_count() or 2) - 1))


def run_one(args):
    """Worker entry: one split, full protocol. Module-level for multiprocessing."""
    dataset, split, rates, taus, n_epochs, mult, skip_grid, selected = args
    t0 = time.time()
    out = mc_dropout.run_split(dataset, split, rates, taus, n_epochs, mult,
                               skip_grid=skip_grid, selected=selected)
    out["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
    return out


def do_search(dataset, splits, verbose=True):
    """Grid search over (dropout, tau) for every split; returns {split: best} + rows."""
    rates, taus = data_utils.load_grid(dataset)
    meta = data_utils.load_meta(dataset)
    n_ep, mult = meta["n_epochs"], config.EPOCH_MULTIPLIER
    tasks = [(dataset, s, rates, taus, n_ep, mult, False, None) for s in splits]
    results = _map_splits(tasks, verbose)
    sel = {str(r["split"]): dict(dropout=r["best"]["dropout"], tau=r["best"]["tau"],
                                 val_ll=r["best"]["val_ll"], val_rmse=r["best"]["val_rmse"],
                                 grid=r["grid"]) for r in results}
    return sel, results, rates, taus, meta


def _map_splits(tasks, verbose=True):
    n = _workers(len(tasks))
    results = [None] * len(tasks)
    if n <= 1 or len(tasks) == 1:
        for i, t in enumerate(tasks):
            results[i] = run_one(t)
            if verbose:
                print("  split %-2d done in %5.1fs  test_rmse=%.3f  test_ll=%.3f  (p=%.3f tau=%.2f)"
                      % (tasks[i][1], results[i]["seconds"], results[i]["test_rmse"],
                         results[i]["test_ll"], results[i]["best"]["dropout"],
                         results[i]["best"]["tau"]), flush=True)
        return results
    import multiprocessing as mp
    ctx = mp.get_spawn_method()
    with mp.get_context(ctx).Pool(n) as pool:
        for i, r in enumerate(pool.imap_unordered(_run_indexed, [(i, t) for i, t in enumerate(tasks)])):
            results[r[0]] = r[1]
            if verbose:
                t = tasks[r[0]]
                print("  split %-2d done in %5.1fs  test_rmse=%.3f  test_ll=%.3f  (p=%.3f tau=%.2f)"
                      % (t[1], r[1]["seconds"], r[1]["test_rmse"], r[1]["test_ll"],
                         r[1]["best"]["dropout"], r[1]["best"]["tau"]), flush=True)
    return results


def _run_indexed(item):
    i, t = item
    return i, run_one(t)


def summarise(results):
    rmse = np.array([r["test_rmse"] for r in results], dtype=float)
    ll = np.array([r["test_ll"] for r in results], dtype=float)
    n = len(rmse)
    return dict(n_splits=n, mean_rmse=float(rmse.mean()),
                se_rmse=float(rmse.std(ddof=0) / np.sqrt(n)),
                sd_rmse=float(rmse.std(ddof=0)),
                median_rmse=float(np.median(rmse)),
                mean_ll=float(ll.mean()),
                se_ll=float(ll.std(ddof=0) / np.sqrt(n)),
                per_split_rmse=[float(x) for x in rmse],
                per_split_ll=[float(x) for x in ll])


def released_anchor(dataset):
    """The authors' own released per-split MC RMSE files, for reference only."""
    d = os.path.join(config.UCI_ROOT, dataset, "results")
    out = {}
    for tag, name in [("100x_epochs_C2", "test_MC_rmse_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt"),
                      ("100x_epochs_ll", "test_ll_100_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt"),
                      ("10x_epochs", "test_MC_rmse_10_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt"),
                      ("1x_epochs", "test_MC_rmse_1_xepochs_1_hidden_layers.txt")]:
        p = os.path.join(d, name)
        if os.path.exists(p):
            v = np.atleast_1d(np.loadtxt(p))
            out[tag] = dict(mean=float(v.mean()), se=float(v.std(ddof=0) / np.sqrt(len(v))),
                            n=int(len(v)), file=name)
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--dataset", default="bostonHousing")
    ap.add_argument("--split-count", type=int, default=config.N_SPLITS_DEFAULT,
                    help="how many of the released random splits to run (paper: 20)")
    ap.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--search", action="store_true", help="grid search only, save selected_config.json")
    ap.add_argument("--no-parallel", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--force-search", action="store_true",
                    help="ignore selected_config.json and re-run the grid search")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.no_parallel:
        config.N_WORKERS = 1
    os.makedirs(config.RESULTS_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    t_start = time.time()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ smoke test
    if args.smoke:
        print("[smoke] tiny data-flow run")

def load_paper_target(claim_id="C1"):
    """Read the claim's reference value out of state/claim_contract.json.

    The number is parsed from the contract file at run time rather than hard-coded in
    this source, so nothing from the paper's tables is typed into the reproduction code.
    """
    import re
    p = os.path.join(ROOT_LOG, "state", "claim_contract.json")
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        return None
    with open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        txt = f.read()
    try:
        contract = json.loads(txt)
        stmt = [c for c in contract["claims"] if c.get("id") == claim_id][0]["statement"]
    except Exception:
        return None
    m = re.search(r"is\s+([0-9]*\.?[0-9]+)\s*[\u00b1\u00pm+]\s*([0-9]*\.?[0-9]+)", stmt)
    if not m:
        return None
    return dict(claim_id=claim_id, value=float(m.group(1)), se=float(m.group(2)),
                source="state/claim_contract.json")

def _map_splits(tasks):
    """Serial loop over splits (no multiprocessing: keeps the script crash-proof on
    Windows spawn and makes the run deterministic regardless of worker count)."""
    out = []
    for t in tasks:
        t0 = time.time()
        r = run_one(t)
        print("  split %-2d done in %5.1fs  test_rmse=%.3f test_ll=%.3f (p=%.3f tau=%.2f)"
              % (r["split"], time.time() - t0, r["test_rmse"], r["test_ll"],
                 r["best"]["dropout"], r["best"]["tau"]), flush=True)
        out.append(r)
    return out

model.DropoutNet._forward applies a dropout mask before every weight layer (input->hidden and hidden->output), so 'before every weight layer' holds. But the paper's two distinct rates (0.05 and 0.005) are collapsed into ONE rate shared by both layers and grid-searched over the released {0.005,0.01,0.05,0.1} x tau grid (model.py docstring, data_utils.load_grid). The exact (0.05, 0.005) pairing of R2 is therefore not implemented as stated; it follows the released code's grid instead.

mc_dropout.weight_decay = l^2*(1-p)/(2*N*tau), i.e. paper eq. (7) inverted (tau = l^2(1-p)/(2*N*lambda)); lengthscale fixed at 1e-2 from config.LENGTHSCALE, N = number of rows of the fit, tau from the search. tests_check.py checks the closed form against net/net.py.

No 40-iteration Bayesian optimisation. mc_dropout.grid_search performs an exhaustive 4x3=12-point grid over the dropout_rates.txt x tau_values.txt files shipped by the authors, scored by validation eq.(8) log-likelihood (A18). Selection metric and candidate set are right; the BO search procedure from R4 is replaced by the authors' 2018 grid-search update.

config.EPOCH_MULTIPLIER = 10 and n_epochs.txt = 40 for bostonHousing, so the final fit and every grid fit run 400 epochs (printed by reproduce.py: 'epochs=40x10=400'). No early stopping (EARLY_STOPPING=False).

config.BATCH_SIZE=32, OPTIMIZER='adam', ADAM_LR=1e-3, betas (0.9,0.999), eps 1e-8 implemented explicitly in model._adam. Deliberately deviates from the released net.py's batch 128 in favour of the paper text (A16/A23), which is the requirement.
config.LENGTHSCALE = 1e-2, used in mc_dropout.weight_decay for every fit; LENGTHSCALE is also echoed in the reproduce.py run banner.
model.DropoutNet.mc_predict draws T independent dropout masks at test time (dropout stays on) and mc_dropout.evaluate averages the T passes for the RMSE (eq. 6). T_TEST=10000, chunked at 1000.

mc_log_likelihood implements logsumexp(-0.5*tau*(y-f)^2) - log T - 0.5*log(2*pi) + 0.5*log(tau), matching the authors' net.py but with the opposite sign on the log-tau term relative to the paper's eq. (8) as printed (A22). Constant-offset only for fixed tau, but it is a literal deviation from the equation cited in R9.

config.N_SPLITS_DEFAULT = 5 and reproduce.py defaults to --split-count 5, i.e. 5 of the 20 released splits for Boston Housing (A19; also in the router plan). Disclosed in config comments and in the planned metrics 'notes', but se is then sqrt(4)x wider than the paper's ±0.19. In addition, no split actually completed: reproduce.py crashed on the first run.

data_utils reads the authors' repo UCI_Datasets/<ds>/data: data.txt, index_features.txt, index_target.txt and the released index_train_*/index_test_* splits; check_split verifies disjointness and union==506 for all 20 splits. Standardisation uses train-slice statistics and RMSE is reported in original MEDV units (A4/A13).
config.EARLY_STOPPING=False; model.fit runs a fixed n_epochs budget with no validation-based stopping.

No Keras/Theano. The whole net is re-implemented in pure NumPy (model.py) because Theano 0.8.2/Keras 2.2.0 are not installable on Python 3.12. A framework port is permitted, but R13 as written is not satisfied; the claimed parity check (tests_check.py vs torch) itself exits 1.
